subject: Retention & backup purge — proposed timeline and DPA callouts
body:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@medtechco.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medtechco.com
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: retention window & backup purge — ask from legal

Hi Vivek,

Legal and IT at MedTechCo are finalizing our DPA checklist and have two items where we need concrete answers for procurement sign-off:

1) Confirm the guaranteed deletion window from our API request for customer data and the maximum time data may remain in offline backups.
2) Describe exception handling for legal holds and how long logs/forensic copies can be retained if a preservation request is in place.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with the questions split by environment (prod, staging, backups). Can someone from Redwood confirm concrete timelines and the process for initiating a purge from backups (if allowed under the DPA)?

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of IT Compliance
MedTechCo

Attachment: backup-delete-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

-----Original Message-----

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@medtechco.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:08:32 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: retention window & backup purge — ask from legal

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in our Legal and Product folks to make sure we provide an operationally actionable response. Summary below; full details and attachments attached.

Key points (high level):
- Online/primary data: deletion request processed and objects removed from primary stores within 24–72 hours; metadata tombstones propagated within 48 hours.
- Backups: we keep 30-day rolling snapshots for primary clusters by default. Backups are immutable for the snapshot retention window; scheduled snapshot deletion happens at day 31 automatically.
- Emergency/exception purges: for confirmed DPA-allowed purges we can initiate targeted restore-and-delete operations; full backup-level purge to remove historical snapshot copies requires coordination with our storage provider and is typically a 2–6 week operation depending on geographic replication.
- Legal holds: when a preservation request is issued, snapshots and logs are flagged and excluded from normal lifecycle deletion; retention can be extended to match legal hold duration, with audit logs noting the extension.

Actions I propose:
1) Kimberley from Legal (cc) will call out any contractual DPA language we need to confirm or limit.
2) Marcus (ops) will validate the 2–6 week timeline for backup purge for US regions and outline the exact steps.
3) I will prepare an appendix showing the end-to-end timeline and the operational ticketing/process for an emergency purge.

I've attached an initial draft response (redwood-data-retention-ask.pdf) for your legal review. Happy to hop on a call next week to walk through.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-retention-ask.pdf (PDF stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial: retention window & backup purge — ask from legal

Samantha — quick legal clarifications inline and a couple of required DPA caveats:

On 2 Nov 2027, Vivek Kulkarni wrote:
> - Backups: we keep 30-day rolling snapshots for primary clusters by default. Backups are immutable for the snapshot retention window; scheduled snapshot deletion happens at day 31 automatically.

We confirm the 30-day default, but legal wants two additions reflected in contract language:
1) A carve-out: data subject requests that are subject to a lawful preservation (e.g., litigation hold) will suspend the 30-day automatic deletion for the affected object keys. We will mark snapshots by object id and exclude them from automatic deletion.
2) Deletion from backups: Redwood commits to making commercially reasonable efforts to remove customer data from backup snapshots when a verified deletion request is received and there is no legal hold. However, because backups are immutable and geo-replicated, we need a clause that the customer accepts a best-effort timeline (we propose 2–6 weeks for the US region) and that deletion completion will be confirmed by a signed attestation (e.g., DocuSign) provided after the operation completes.

Additionally, we need to add a short section on logging:
- For forensic logs, default retention is 180 days. Logs that are subject to investigation or compliance review may be retained longer; retention extension will be documented and an internal approvals trail will be recorded.

Marcus — please confirm the proposed 2–6 week purge window below is accurate operationally for US multi-AZ clusters.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial: retention window & backup purge — ask from legal

Samantha — operational confirmation below. Apologies for the longer reply; I validated with Storage and Replication teams.

Operational confirmation (US region, multi-AZ):
- Snapshot retention: 30-day rolling, immutable snapshots as Vivek noted.
- Backup purge for deletion requests (no legal hold): we perform a targeted restore of the affected keyspace, remove the object from the primary copy, and then run a purge routine across snapshot manifests to flag the object for deletion. Because snapshots are replicated, we coordinate across 3 cloud regions/AZs — typical calendar time: 10–28 days depending on window scheduling and storage vendor job backlog.
- If the customer requires a faster removal, we can escalate to an expedited purge; typical expedited SLA is 5–10 business days but requires a written request and an operational fee stated in the DPA addendum.
- For logs: default 180 days retention; for forensics we can create secured forensic exports which are retained only under a documented legal hold; export copies are air-gapped and only accessible to the legal/ops team handling the hold.

I will attach a short runbook and the job checklist to the ticket once we kick off.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Please add the expedited purge fee and the 5–10 business day SLA into the DPA addendum (we will route internally if acceptable).
2) Can Redwood provide the attestation template you mentioned for verification once a purge completes? We prefer DocuSign execution for the attestation.
3) For logs — can you confirm the process for requesting a forensic export and whether MedTechCo will receive a signed chain-of-custody record?

If you can share the attestation template and the runbook checklist (even redacted) we can turn this into an internal approval package. If everything looks good we'll sign the DPA addendum and route DocuSign for the attestation when the first purge is scheduled.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
